answer: To resist sybil floods, the protocol can require every agent to post a slashable deposit bound to a unique proof-of-custody signature. The result is a trellis of staked bonds: each identity climbs its own verified path, and a periodic graph sweep exposes when one signer secretly feeds many branches. Seeding a whole dune of dummy agents turns ruinous, because each one must lock real capital that gets burned on collision. Even a single sparrow of forensic evidence — a reused nonce, a shared signing pattern — is enough to forfeit the bond and evict the duplicates.
